issues.description: Template provides a class named AnimalFarm in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, while the problem statement and solution expect a class named Farm. This mismatch in class name and file content will confuse students and prevent them from implementing or compiling the required Farm API described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the template file content so it declares public class Farm in package de.tum.cit.ase (not AnimalFarm) and provide the expected fields/methods (List<Animal> animals, addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong, singFarmSongVerse). Ensure the class name matches the file name Farm.java to align with the problem statement and solution.

issues.description: The template Farm.java file contains malformed and duplicated code (e.g., a package declaration embedded inside a method body, duplicated class blocks, and mismatched braces) which will cause compile errors and block students from building and running the project. These structural errors are unintentional and prevent following the intended exercise flow.
issues.suggestedFix: Clean up the template Farm.java by removing duplicated blocks and misplaced package declarations. Provide a single well-formed public class Farm in the file with proper package declaration at the top, correct imports, matching braces, and TODO stubs where appropriate. Use the solution Farm.java as a structural reference so the template compiles and students can focus on the intended exercises.

issues.description: The template repository defines the farm class as 'AnimalFarm' (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) while the problem statement and the solution use the identifier 'Farm'. This mismatch between the expected class name 'Farm' (used throughout the UML, tasks, and solution) and the template's 'AnimalFarm' creates a direct mapping conflict: students following the instructions will look for/instantiate 'Farm' but the template provides a different class name, causing compilation errors and confusion about the required entity.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template file to match the problem statement and solution: change 'public class AnimalFarm' to 'public class Farm' (and ensure the filename remains Farm.java). Remove any stray/duplicate package declarations inside methods and align the class API (constructors, methods) with the UML and solution so students can directly map 'Farm' from the problem to the template implementation.
